blocks.text: This is a directory of 71 mobile home and manufactured home parks from Surrey and Coquitlam to Hope, grouped by area. The list is compiled from public park and listing information; there is no official registry of parks, so check a park’s name and address with the park before you visit.

faq.q: How many mobile home parks are in this directory?
faq.a: 71 parks across Abbotsford, Agassiz, Chilliwack, Coquitlam, Cultus Lake, Hope, Langley, Maple Ridge, Mission, Rosedale, Ruskin and Surrey. It is not an official registry, so confirm a park’s details with the park.

faq.q: How much is pad rent in Fraser Valley parks?
faq.a: It depends on the park. The figure that matters is the rent in the specific park’s written tenancy agreement for that site.

faq.q: How much can pad rent rise?
faq.a: Once every 12 months with at least 3 full months’ notice, capped by a formula: 2.3% plus a proportional amount in 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount in 2027. There is no rounding up and no carry-forward.

faq.q: Do I own land when I buy a park home?
faq.a: On a rented pad, no. You own the home and rent the pad, and the site right is the tenancy assigned to you. Bare-land strata and co-op communities work differently.

faq.q: Does the park have to approve my purchase?
faq.a: Yes. The park owner’s prior written consent is needed, requested on Form 10. A response is due by the 10th day, silence counts as consent, no fee can be charged, and the pad rent and next increase date carry over.

faq.q: What happens if the park is sold or converted to another use?
faq.a: The owner must first have all required government permits and approvals, give 12 months’ notice and pay $20,000 on or before the effective date. The tenant can leave early on 10 days’ notice, has 15 days to dispute, and may be eligible for further compensation through dispute resolution.

faq.q: Are there market statistics for Fraser Valley mobile homes?
faq.a: Not as a separate category. Fraser Valley market reports cover houses, townhomes and condos, so they do not describe park homes.
